label: GO after rewarded S2 (esp. a2), growing with episode trial, off after trial ~85
terms: (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * np.minimum(ep_trial, 80) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 2) * np.minimum(ep_trial, 80) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 1) * np.minimum(ep_trial, 80) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_trial >= 85) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.clip(-belief_lo, 0, 6) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * (ep_trial >= 85) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == -1) * (prev_reward == 1) * (1 - belief) * np.minimum(ep_trial, 80)
explanation: Fires only at GO. Magnitude = (previous trial reached S2 and was rewarded) x a ramp in episode trial (rises to ~trial 80, collapses after ~85). Slope is about 2x larger after a2->S2 common rewarded than after a1->S2 rare rewarded. All other previous-trial patterns sit at ~0, so a term that cancels the additive timing baseline at GO matters. Given S2-rewarded, stronger ideal-observer certainty that S2 is good slightly lowers it. On the window's first trial (previous state unknown, previous reward 1), (1 - belief) x ramp stands in for 'last outcome was S2 rewarded'. No future, hidden or model-output variables used. Dev R2 beyond timing 0.776, test 0.773, above the profile's additive 'all' ceiling (0.56) because of the multiplicative last-trial x episode-time structure. The earlier model-based firing label (GO after a2 S2 r, choosing a2) is matched by observed quantities alone with no loss.

issues: "Off after ~85" is wrong as stated. Splitting the trials after an S2-rewarded trial into 3-trial bins on top of a min(ep_trial,80) ramp (slope 0.0056, peak about 0.45) gives these offsets: 80-83 +0.01, 83-86 -0.02, 86-89 -0.09, 89-92 -0.15, 92-95 -0.28, 95-98 -0.43, 98-100 -0.48. So the feature is still fully on at 85-86, about half on near trial 92, and only off from about trial 95.

The worst-fit windows from misses are mostly late in the episode, where the step term (ep_trial >= 85, weight -0.345) predicts about 0 but the feature fires strongly. Examples: t85 a2 after a1 S2R r, actual 1.03 vs predicted 0.03; t92 after a1 S2R r, actual 0.94 vs -0.08; t89, actual 0.31 vs 0.05.

Swapping the step for a gradual decline, np.clip(ep_trial-82,0,16), and applying it also to the first-trial proxy, raises R^2 beyond timing from 0.773 to 0.810 on test (0.818 dev). That is a real systematic gain, though modest.

Other claims check out. The a2->S2 slope is about twice the a1->S2 slope (0.0094 vs 0.0049). The belief term matters only slightly: removing it costs 0.005 on test. The first-trial (prev_state == -1) proxy matters a lot: removing it drops test R^2 from 0.768 to 0.566.

There is no large hidden factor beyond what the terms already cover. The upcoming choice (action == 2) adds 0.004 on test. Belief within a1 S2 r adds 0.001 or less, and two-back history adds 0.005 or less. Misses by phase and previous trial show only residuals of 0.007 or smaller.
